title: Ephemeral analytics views: privacy-stamping, scrub-tokens, and retireable export manifest
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Add a first-class primitive to the console analytics pipeline: Ephemeral Aggregation Views (EAVs). EAVs are short-lived, queryable artifacts produced by the aggregation layer that are privacy-stamped, optionally encrypted, and bound to a retirement manifest. The feature enables safe ad-hoc exports, internal dashboards, and third-party delivery while ensuring scrubbing and provable deletion semantics (audit ledger entries + verifiable TTL). This ticket covers schema changes, pipeline transforms, retention enforcement, API surface, and an audit trail for deletion attestations.
acceptance_criteria: Create EAV producer stage in the ingestion pipeline producing privacy-stamped manifests with schema versioning
EAVs must support per-customer TTL and per-export scrub-token rules; when TTL expires the view is deleted and an attest record is appended to the audit ledger
Console backend exposes GET /exports/{id} and DELETE /exports/{id} with RBAC checks and returns deletion attestations
Automated job verifies physical removal from object storage and warehouse within SLA window and marks state in metadata store
End-to-end test covering export creation -> scrubbing -> expiration -> attestations passes in staging and is wired into deploy pipeline
migration_steps: Add exports_metadata table (export_id, owner_id, schema_v, privacy_stamp, ttl, storage_path, state, created_at, deleted_at) with backfill script to copy recent ad-hoc exports
Deploy pipeline transformer that emits privacy_stamp header into export manifests (small migration deploy A/Bable)
Enable read-only console endpoint for new manifest format, then cutover producers
Backfill TTL for existing exports using conservative 30-day default and enqueue retire tasks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable EAV producer for internal analytics team only; monitor cost and deletion failures
Phase 2: opt-in for customers via console toggle; require legal/PO acceptance for high-risk datasets
Phase 3: default on with per-team quotas and auto-retire policies; document in customer-facing privacy docs
testing_plan: Unit tests for privacy_stamp generation and verification
Integration tests that simulate export creation, storage to S3, TTL expiry, and audit ledger append
Chaos test: simulate exporter retries and stale manifest versions to validate idempotency
Compliance test: generate attestations and verify they match physical object removal using checksum
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: exports.retire.success_count and exports.retire.failure_count (alert if failure_count > 5 in 15m)
SLO: 99.9% of expired EAVs must be physically removed within 24 hours of TTL
